description: Hands-on PC and laptop hardware: what every component does, how to choose, assemble, configure and repair a machine, and how to install and tune the operating system on it. Taught to the depth of the professional hardware technician certification, with every procedure practised on real or virtual machines.
modelledOn: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1101) hardware and networking objectives
Andrews, Dark and West, CompTIA A+ Guide to IT Technical Support
outcomes: Identify every component on a motherboard and explain how CPU, chipset, memory and buses connect.
Choose and install processors, memory, storage, power supplies and expansion cards that are compatible with one another.
Configure BIOS/UEFI, boot order, secure boot and firmware updates safely.
Install and configure operating systems, drivers and printers on desktops and laptops.
Diagnose hardware faults with a repeatable troubleshooting procedure and basic tools.
Specify a custom build for a stated budget and workload, including power and thermal limits.

units.title: Safety, tools and the anatomy of a PC
topics: Electrostatic discharge, mains safety, lifting and handling; the technician toolkit
Form factors: ATX, micro-ATX, mini-ITX, SFF; case airflow
Tour of a disassembled desktop: identifying every part and cable
Documenting a system: inventory, serial numbers, photographs before disassembly

units.title: Motherboards, processors and memory
topics: Motherboard layout: sockets, chipset, VRMs, slots, headers, jumpers; reading the manual
CPU basics for technicians: cores, threads, clock, cache, TDP, integrated graphics; Intel and AMD sockets
Installing a CPU, thermal paste and coolers; air versus liquid cooling; thermal throttling
DRAM: DDR4 and DDR5, DIMM and SO-DIMM, channels, ECC, XMP/EXPO profiles; installing and testing RAM
Buses and interfaces: PCIe lanes and generations, SATA, M.2, USB versions, Thunderbolt

units.title: Storage devices and power supplies
topics: Hard disks, SATA and NVMe SSDs, flash wear, SMART data; RAID 0, 1, 5, 10
Partitioning (MBR, GPT), file systems (NTFS, FAT32, exFAT, ext4) and cloning a drive
Power supply ratings, 80 Plus efficiency, rails, connectors, modular supplies; calculating a wattage budget
Uninterruptible power supplies and surge protection for unstable mains; testing a PSU
Backup media and external storage

units.title: Expansion, peripherals and display devices
topics: Graphics cards: GPU, VRAM, outputs, power and slot requirements; installing and testing
Sound, network, capture and other expansion cards; USB and wireless peripherals
Display technologies: LCD (TN, IPS, VA), OLED, refresh rate, resolution, colour depth; projectors
Video interfaces: HDMI, DisplayPort, DVI, VGA, USB-C alt mode; multi-monitor setup and calibration
Keyboards, mice, scanners, webcams, barcode and smart-card readers; KVM switches
Connectors and cables: identifying, testing and replacing them

units.title: BIOS/UEFI, firmware and boot
topics: POST, beep and LED codes; BIOS and UEFI settings, boot order, secure boot, TPM, virtualisation flags
Firmware updates and recovery; CMOS battery and resetting settings
Boot process from firmware to bootloader to kernel; UEFI partitions
Overclocking, fan curves and power limits: what is safe

units.title: Installing operating systems
topics: Creating installation media; clean install, upgrade, image deployment
Installing Windows and a Linux distribution; dual boot and partitioning
Drivers, Windows Update and package managers; activation and licensing
Post-install tasks: user accounts, security updates, antivirus, backup, restore points
Virtual machines as a safe way to practise installations
Recovery tools: safe mode, recovery environment, bootable rescue media

units.title: Installing and configuring printers
topics: Laser, inkjet, thermal and 3D printer technologies and consumables
Local, network and wireless printer installation; drivers and print queues
Sharing a printer, print servers, printing from phones
Common faults: paper jams, streaks, blank pages, offline printers; preventive maintenance

units.title: Laptops and mobile devices
topics: Laptop anatomy: batteries, chargers, keyboards, displays, hinges, SO-DIMMs, M.2 drives
Disassembly technique and manufacturer service manuals; replacing a screen, battery and keyboard
Power management, battery health and charging circuits
Docking stations, port replicators and wireless cards; phones and tablets basics

units.title: Custom configurations
topics: Matching a build to a workload: office, gaming, CAD, video editing, virtualisation host, small server, thin client
Compatibility checking: socket, chipset, RAM, PSU, case clearance, PCIe lanes
Costing a build in cedis from local and online suppliers; import and warranty considerations
Benchmarking and burn-in testing a new machine

units.title: Troubleshooting
topics: A six-step troubleshooting method: identify, theorise, test, plan, implement, verify and document
No-power, no-POST, no-display, overheating, random reboots, blue screens, slow performance
Diagnostic tools: multimeter, POST card, memory test, disk health, stress tests, event logs
Preventive maintenance in dusty and humid conditions; cleaning and thermal servicing
Writing a repair report and talking to a non-technical user
